items.title: Retirement: Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps
items.description:
The Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps will be retired on September 29, 2027. After this date, existing Functions v1 apps on Azure Container Apps will stop running and will no longer process requests or event-driven triggers. 

This retirement applies to the hosting model on Azure Container Apps, not the programming model version used by your function code. 

Action required 

Review your Azure environments and migrate all affected apps to the Functions v2 hosting model before September 29, 2027 to avoid service disruption. 

Functions v2 uses a native Azure Container App configured with `kind=functionapp`. You can reuse your existing container image; the standard migration path doesn't require function code changes. 

Use the Azure Functions on Azure Container Apps v1 migration assistant to help migrate your function apps from the v1 model to the v2 model. 

To migrate manually 

1. Record the v1 app's configuration, including secrets, identity, networking, and scaling. 

2. Create a v2 app with `kind=functionapp` and reapply the configuration. 

3. Test all triggers, shift production traffic, and then decommission the v1 app. 

We recommend completing migration and production validation well before the retirement date. 

For assistance, contact your Microsoft account team or create an Azure support request.  

Learn more: 

  • Migrate to Azure Functions v2 on Azure Container Apps 
  • Create an Azure Functions app with auto scaling rules on Azure Container Apps

items.title: Generally Available: Storage optimized Lasv5 and Laosv5 Azure VM series
items.description:
The Laosv5 series and Lasv5 storage optimized VMs, based on the 5th Gen AMD EPYC™ processor (Turin), are now generally available.

Lasv5 and Laosv5 VMs have sizes ranging from 2-160 vCPUs, with 8GiB of memory and 720GB of local NVMe disk capacity per vCPU.  Both support 200Gbps of network bandwidth and deliver up to 35% better average CPU performance. The Lasv5 VMs offer up to 30.7TB of local storage capacity with 9.6M read IOPS performance, while the Laosv5 VMs offer up to 138TB of local storage capacity with 20.7M read IOPS performance.

These VM series are powered by Azure Boost and Azure Boost SSDs, enable NVMe local SSD disk encryption by default, and come with an NVMe remote storage interface with support for premium storage caching, significantly improving remote storage performance.

Compared to the previous generation Lasv4 VMs, Lasv5 VMs have:

  • 33% larger maximum local storage capacity

  • 9% larger temp disk random read IOPS per vCPU

  • New 128 and 160 vCPU sizes

Compared to the previous generation Laosv4 VMs, Laosv5 VMs have:

  • 500% larger maximum local storage capacity

  • 619% larger maximum read IOPS

  • New 48, 64, 96, 128, and160 vCPU sizes

All L-series v5 VMs are perfect for distributed, scale-out workloads that require high amounts of local storage capacity per vCPU and the ability to move that data quickly over the network or to an Azure remote storage backend.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Automatic Zone Placement for Virtual Machine Scale Sets
items.description:
Automatic Zone Placement for VM Scale Sets (Public Preview) enables Azure to automatically select the best availability zones for your scale set based on SKU availability, capacity, and placement requirements. Instead of manually maintaining zone lists for each region, customers can use a consistent configuration across regions while Azure handles zone selection.

Key benefits include:

  • Simplified multi-region deployments with no region-specific zone management.
  • Capacity-aware zone selection to improve deployment and scale-out success.
  • Flexible resiliency controls that let you define zone spread and per-zone capacity limits.
  • Greater allocation flexibility by allowing Azure to use additional eligible zones when needed.
  • Support for both new and existing VM Scale Sets using Uniform or Flexible orchestration modes.

By default, Automatic Zone Placement distributes instances evenly across three availability zones, maintains a minimum spread across two zones, limits any single zone to 50% of total instances, and can expand into additional zones if required for scaling. Customers can further customize eligible zones, zone count, balancing behavior, and capacity distribution to meet workload needs.

The feature only affects placement of new VM instances and does not rebalance existing VMs. Existing deployments can use Automatic Zone Balance to correct zone imbalances.

Automatic Zone Placement is available in public preview through the Azure portal, CLI, PowerShell, and REST API. To get started, register the Microsoft.Compute/VmssAutomaticZonePlacement AFEC, use Compute API version March 1, 2026 or later, and configure a VM Scale Set with the Auto zone placement policy.

items.description:

items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Ultra Disk
items.description:
Ultra Disk support is now available in public preview for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. You can use Azure’s highest-performance managed disk option for I/O-intensive and transaction-heavy PostgreSQL workloads that require consistently low sub-millisecond latency, high IOPS, and throughput. With independently configurable capacity and performance, you can align storage needs more closely with your workload requirements.   

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: SQL Performance Monitoring for Azure SQL Database
items.description:
The public preview of Microsoft-managed performance monitoring for Azure SQL Database is now available.  

You can now monitor Azure SQL Database without building custom collection scripts or correlating telemetry across disconnected tools. Built-in data collection sends performance telemetry from your databases to a Microsoft-managed telemetry pipeline for processing and storage.  

Resource-level and estate-wide dashboards help you identify performance trends, anomalies, and resource bottlenecks. Integration with Fabric Database Hub brings this telemetry into a unified, estate-level monitoring experience. For deeper analysis and custom visualizations, you can securely query your data with Kusto Query Language through an RBAC-protected Azure Data Explorer proxy endpoint.  

Learn more:  

  • Documentation  
  • Announcement blog

items.title: Public Preview: Performance monitoring for Azure Arc–enabled SQL Server
items.description:
The preview of performance monitoring for SQL Server enabled by Azure Arc is expanding with more flexible ways to explore and visualize your performance data. You can query Microsoft-managed monitoring data directly through a telemetry endpoint. The built-in Azure portal experience now uses Grafana dashboards, providing ready-to-use views without requiring you to deploy and manage a monitoring pipeline.  

You can also connect your own Grafana environment to the same telemetry endpoint and build dashboards tailored to your operational needs. Integration with Fabric Database Hub brings this telemetry into a unified, estate-level monitoring experience. This update helps provide a unified view of health and performance across your Azure database estate, eliminating the need to monitor databases one instance at a time.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for late-September 2026
items.description:
The following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:   

  • Scale larger workloads on Azure SQL Database Hyperscale Premium series with new 160-vCore and 192-vCore options, delivering up to 50% greater compute capacity than the previous 128-vCore maximum.  
  • Enable automatic index compaction to reduce storage space consumption and save resources without index maintenance jobs.  
  • Query and explore Azure SQL Database directly from the Azure portal with the modern, browser-based SQL Query Editor, without requiring external tools.  
  • Make informed Azure SQL migration decisions directly within SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) with intelligent target recommendations tailored to your workload.  
  • Get enhanced state management for improved performance and responsiveness with the new Results Grid experience, now with expanded column customization options.  
  • Run the built-in SQL formatter on demand in SSMS, configuring for automatic formatting on save, and customizing through SSMS settings or .editorconfig files.  
  • Compare two database definitions with Schema Compare. The source and target of the comparison can be any combination of connected database, SQL database project, or .dacpac file.  
  • Now write one set of connection string keywords and use them across our Microsoft SQL drivers. No more looking up connection string keywords for every different language or framework that you work with.  

Learn more: 

  • New 160-vCore and 192-vCore options 
  • Enable automatic index compaction  
  • Query and explore Azure SQL Database directly from the Azure portal with SQL Query Editor 
  •  SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) with intelligent target recommendations  
  • Expanded column customization options with Results Grid 
  • Run the built-in SQL formatter on demand in SSMS 
  • Compare two database definitions with Schema Compare

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK)
items.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK). You can encrypt your data using keys stored in an Azure Key Vault or Azure Managed HSM that resides in a different Microsoft Entra tenant than your PostgreSQL server. This update is ideal for SaaS providers and ISVs that need to keep database operations and key ownership in separate tenants. 

With cross-tenant CMK, you can keep full control of your encryption keys while applications and databases run in a service provider's tenant. This separation helps you meet security and compliance requirements by keeping key management independent from service operations, while allowing you to manage key rotation and revocation on your terms. 

Learn more

products: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
items.title: Public preview: Script-based deployment for SQL Server on Linux Azure VM
items.description:
A new deployment experience for SQL Server on Linux Azure Virtual Machines (VMs) replaces legacy marketplace images with automated script-based provisioning. This release provides greater flexibility, simplified management, and improved customization. You can deploy a standard Linux VM, configure SQL Server, and automatically install and register SQL Server through an integrated workflow. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SQL Server on Azure Local Disconnected (ALDO)
items.description:
Now you can use ALDO to extend SQL Server support to environments that can’t maintain continuous connectivity to Azure. ALDO is designed for operations in highly regulated, secure, remote, or air-gapped environments, where internet connectivity is restricted or unavailable. SQL Server workloads continue to run entirely on Azure Local infrastructure while maintaining operational independence from cloud connectivity. 

In addition to traditional database workloads, you can use ALDO to support local AI and intelligent application scenarios in disconnected environments. By keeping data, AI models, and SQL Server workloads within the same secure infrastructure boundary, you can build and run AI-powered solutions without requiring cloud connectivity. This is particularly valuable for defense, government, manufacturing, energy, and remote-edge deployments where data sovereignty, security, and operational continuity are critical requirements. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SQL Server support on Azure Local connected mode
items.description:
With SQL Server on Azure Local, you can run SQL Server workloads on Azure Local infrastructure while leveraging Azure services for centralized management, governance, monitoring, security, and licensing experiences. By connecting to Azure through Azure Arc, you can maintain a consistent hybrid operating model across on-premises, edge, and cloud environments.  

In addition to traditional database workloads, you can use SQL Server on Azure Local to provide a foundation for AI-powered applications and intelligent data solutions. You can keep sensitive data local while enabling AI and analytics scenarios that require low-latency access to operational data. This approach helps you bring AI closer to the data, reducing data movement while supporting governance and compliance requirements. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for late-September 2026
items.description:
In late September 2026, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:  

  • Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric is a unified experience for discovering, managing, monitoring, and optimizing databases across SQL Server, Azure SQL, PostgreSQL, Azure Cosmos DB, and Fabric SQL. By bringing AI-powered insights and agents into a single control plane, Database Hub simplifies database operations and helps you modernize your data estate.  
  • You can now increase the number of databases allowed in a Hyperscale Elastic pool to 50.  
  • Azure SQL Database now supports local time zones, enabling applications to operate using a configured time zone without requiring custom logic or workarounds.  
  • The MSSQL extension’s modernized landing page makes it easier to discover features and get started quickly.   
  • You can now use a single Azure SQL Managed Instance link to replicate multiple databases from SQL Server Always On Availability Groups to Azure SQL Managed Instance.  

Learn more: 

  • Data Hub in Microsoft Fabric   
  • Increased databases in Hyperscale Elastic pool  
  • Local time zones in Azure SQL Database  
  • MSSQL extension modernized landing page 
  • Single Azure SQL Managed Instance link to replicate multiple databases

items.title: Generally Available: Database DevOps in SSMS powered by SQL projects
items.description:
In SSMS, you can now use Microsoft.Build.Sql projects to help you implement, manage, and collaborate on database changes, by providing a local definition of the database objects. A SQL database project is a local representation of SQL objects that comprise the schema for a single database, such as tables, stored procedures, or functions. With this support for the development cycle of a SQL database project, you can integrate database development into continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) workflows that are familiar as development best practices. 

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL Database Hyperscale Serverless auto-pause and auto-resume
items.description:
Auto-pause and auto-resume are now available in public preview for Azure SQL Hyperscale databases using the Serverless compute tier. You can configure databases to automatically pause during periods of inactivity and automatically resume when activity returns, helping reduce costs for workloads that experience extended or predictable idle periods.  

When a database is paused, compute billing stops and only storage-related charges continue to apply. Auto-pause and auto-resume can be enabled for both new and existing Azure SQL Hyperscale databases using the Serverless compute tier.  

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SQL Formatter
items.description:
You can now format SQL scripts directly in Visual Studio Code using SQL Formatter for more consistent, readable code. Customizable formatting options help you match your preferred coding style, so you can keep queries tidy without manual reformatting.   

Now available in general availability, this feature makes it easier to standardize SQL across your projects and streamline everyday development.   

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: SQL Migration Agent Skills for assessment, migration, and validation
items.description:
SQL Migration Agent Skills help you automate and streamline the end-to-end migration journey from SQL Server to Azure. These reusable AI-powered skills help guide you through assessment, target selection, migration execution, and post-migration validation, so you can migrate with less manual effort and more confidence. These skills are designed to work across multiple Microsoft user interfaces while preserving migration context, keeping you in control of critical decisions.  

Key capabilities: 

  • Assess readiness and identify blockers by analyzing SQL Server workloads for compatibility issues, risks, and migration challenges. 

  • Recommend the best-fit Azure destination with guidance on Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines, including sizing and suitability considerations. 

  • Automate migration workflows with clear guidance for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance scenarios. 

  • Validate migration success through post-migration verification and remediation guidance to help ensure workload readiness after cutover. 

 Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Arc enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager will be retired September 30, 2029
items.description:
Microsoft is retiring Azure Arc-enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager (SCVMM) in September 2029. Customers must plan and transition to alternative solutions.

What does this mean for you?

If you are using Azure Arc-enabled SCVMM for:
  • Azure services and Azure Arc capabilities such as monitoring, security, governance, updates, and licensing for Extended Security Updates and Pay-as-you-go SQL and WS, we recommend switching to Azure Arc-enabled Servers.
  • VM lifecycle and powercycle operations such as create, start, stop, restart, resize, and self-service VM management, we recommend that you reach out to us through e-mail to arc-vmm-feedback@microsoft.com.
What action should you take?
  1. Review your current use of Azure Arc-enabled SCVMM.
  2. Determine the appropriate migration path: Azure Arc-enabled Servers or if you need help, reach out to Microsoft.
  3. Follow the migration guidance to deboard your SCVMM environment from Azure Arc and onboard to your alternative solution.
We recommend beginning your transition planning as soon as possible to ensure a smooth migration before retirement. You can also share your feedback or any concerns that you may have during this transition through e-mail to arc-vmm-feedback@microsoft.com.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Migrate directly from Azure Arc to Azure SQL Database, including Hyperscale
items.description:
You can now select Azure SQL Database, including Hyperscale, as a migration target directly from the database migration experience in Azure Arc. The workflow brings Azure Database Migration Service and Self-hosted Integration Runtime setup into the guided portal journey, allowing you to assess your SQL Server estate, choose your target, configure your migration and monitor progress without leaving Arc.

Until now, your path from assessment to migration required stepping outside Arc, learning a separate service, configuring a runtime, and moving between multiple tools. This additional effort slowed modernization projects. With this release, the databases Arc already identified as migration-ready become databases you can act on immediately, in the same place you assessed them.

You get the same migration dashboard, monitoring experience, and guided workflow already used for other Azure SQL destinations, so choosing Hyperscale does not require learning a new migration methodology. Runtime setup is guided and completed only once, with in-portal instructions that walk you through the process.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Microsoft SQL Agent Skills
items.description:
Microsoft SQL Agent Skills help you get more accurate, product-specific guidance when using AI agents to build, operate, and migrate SQL workloads. You can use these skills with Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Database container, SQL Server to Azure migration, and Fabric Database Hub scenarios.

The skills provide SQL-specific guidance that helps your AI agent work more effectively with Microsoft SQL technologies, making it easier to complete common development, migration, and management tasks.

Learn more.

items.title: Public Preview: Long-term retention (LTR) v2 for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
items.description:
LTR v2 is the next-generation long-term backup solution for Azure Database for PostgreSQL that moves from logical backups (pg_dump/pg_restore) used in LTR v1 to physical snapshot-based backups integrated with Azure Backup Vaults.  

With this release, you can now support daily backups while gaining much greater scalability for large databases through physical snapshots rather than pg_dump-based exports.  

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Microsoft HPC Pack
items.description:
Microsoft is retiring all versions of HPC Pack. End of Support is August 27, 2027. HPC Pack is now entering a one-year retirement period. Microsoft will provide limited, retirement-only support during this period. The scope of this support is defined below so customers know what to expect. 

In scope until End of Support: 

• Security/CVE response and necessary security updates. 

• Guidance from existing documentation and validated configurations. 

• Assistance with supported components and documented functionality. 

• Case-by-case evaluation of long-term support options where available. 

Out of scope: 

• Non-security fixes or product improvements. 

• New features, custom code, or design changes. 

• Validation of new operating systems, hardware, dependencies, architectures, or integrations. 

• New product investigation or documentation. 

• Migration planning, execution, or consulting. 

• Unsupported configurations. 

After August 27, 2027, HPC Pack will receive no updates, fixes, or technical support. Existing deployments will remain operational but unsupported. 

Required action 

Begin assessing and transitioning workloads now. Consider Azure Batch for managed parallel and HPC scheduling, or another appropriate Azure service. No alternative guarantees one-to-one feature parity. Engage your Microsoft account team or Cloud Solution Architect for planning. 

Share customer needs and transition challenges through this form: ESU Extend Request.

items.title: Retirement: Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029
items.description:
Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029. You can continue using Azure IoT Central until the retirement date, but we recommend starting your transition planning early.

Why is this happening?

As Azure IoT evolves, Microsoft is focusing future investment on Azure IoT platform services that provide greater scalability, architectural flexibility, lifecycle management, and integration with Microsoft Fabric for analytics and AI-driven workloads. Azure IoT Hub, Device Provisioning Service (DPS), and Azure Device Registry represent the recommended Azure-native platform for connected operations.

Recommended action 

  • Review your current Azure IoT Central applications, devices, dashboards, , and integrations.
  • Evaluate Azure IoT Hub and DPS as the target architecture for device connectivity and provisioning.
  • Evaluate Microsoft Fabric for real-time analytics, dashboards, and broader data experiences.
  • Use the Azure IoT Central migration playbook to map existing IoT Central scenarios to Azure IoT services. 
  • Begin planning and executing your transition before September 20, 2029. 
  • If additional assistance is required, engage Microsoft field teams or an Azure IoT migration partner. 

Help and support 

If you have questions, get answers from community experts through Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and need technical assistance, create an Azure support request.

Generally Available: Storage with cool access enhancement
items.description:
QoS update with cool access enabled on Premium and Ultra service levels improves how Azure NetApp Files balances performance and cost for mixed hot and cool workloads. Throughput automatically adjusts as data moves to cool storage, maintaining hot‑tier performance while enabling customers to benefit from cool access at scale. This enhancement continuously optimizes pool and volume throughput as cool access patterns change, delivering a seamless experience without manual tuning. 

Learn more:

  • Azure NetApp Files storage with cool access

items.title: Public Preview : Microsoft entra kerberos authentication for Azure NetApp Files
items.description:
Azure NetApp Files now supports Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication for SMB volumes. The capability enables users with hybrid or cloud-only identities to authenticate through Microsoft Entra ID using cloud-issued Kerberos tickets. This capability removes the requirement for SMB clients to have network line-of-sight to Active Directory Domain Services domain controllers in the authentication path. It helps organizations simplify identity architecture, reduce infrastructure dependencies, and modernize SMB access for hybrid and cloud-first environments.

Learn more:

  • What's new in Azure NetApp Files
  • Understand Microsoft Entra Kerberos with Azure NetApp Files
  • Configure Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication with Azure NetApp Files
  • Troubleshoot Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication for Azure NetApp Files
